questions.prompt: What fundamentally distinguishes a qubit from a classical bit?
options: A qubit stores more than eight bits of data at once
A qubit can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1 until measured
A qubit is always read faster than a bit
A qubit can never produce an error

questions.prompt: When you measure a qubit that is in a superposition, what do you get?
options: Both 0 and 1 at the same time
A single classical outcome (0 or 1), obtained probabilistically
The exact complex amplitudes of the state
Nothing until you measure it a second time

questions.prompt: True or False: quantum computers are expected to replace classical computers for everyday tasks like email and word processing.

options: They run every existing program faster
They use less electricity than laptops
Some problems (simulating quantum systems, factoring large numbers) are intractable for classical computers
They remove the need to write code
